name: David Bowie
hook: Chased Kraftwerk's European electronic sound to Berlin and came back with a trilogy that pointed rock somewhere it hadn't been.
blurb: Bowie has said directly that Kraftwerk's 'Autobahn' pulled his attention back toward a European electronic sound and away from American rock clichés, and that is part of why he moved to Berlin in the late 1970s. With Brian Eno and Tony Visconti he made three albums, Low, Heroes and Lodger (1977 to 1979), that pulled electronic and ambient sounds into rock. They include 'V-2 Schneider', a direct tribute to Kraftwerk's Florian Schneider. This Berlin Trilogy is the clearest meeting point on this map between German electronic music and mainstream rock, and Kraftwerk returned the compliment by naming Bowie and Iggy Pop on 'Trans-Europe Express'.

signatureTracks.title: Space Oddity
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The breakthrough that established Bowie as a shape-shifting art-rock figure years before the Berlin period.

signatureTracks.title: Heroes
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Recorded in Berlin with Eno and Visconti, and the clearest example of Bowie folding Kraftwerk-indebted electronic texture into a rock song without losing the song.
